The Story in the Data

Fall didn’t bring a sales rush — it brought back competition for houses

① Homes sold each month

Sales peaked in June and have cooled since. September was flat with August — and 10% below last September.

 Freehold    Condo

SYNERGY MLS® pull, Jan–Sep 2026.

② Average sale price

Freehold prices turned back up in September. Condos are still sliding — their lowest average since January.

Freehold and condo shown on separate scales. SYNERGY MLS® pull.

③ Share sold over asking

Bidding came back for houses in September. Condos have held near 1 in 8 since February.

Small figures compare with August 2026 (SYNERGY MLS® pull). *Year-over-year compares with TRREB Market Watch, September 2025, same five regions. “Sold over asking” = share of homes that sold above list price (TRREB doesn’t publish it, so no year-over-year).

The average GTA home sold for $51,600 less than a year ago. Semis are the hottest ticket — prices up 8.8% from August and more than 1 in 3 sold over asking — while condo apartments are the only type to slip again month over month and carry the biggest drop from last year.

So what does this mean for you?

If you’re selling
Semi? Consider an offer date.
More than 1 in 3 sold over asking, at 101.5% of list.
Detached? Price at market.
Only 1 in 5 sold over asking. Average sale: 98.1% of list.
Condo? Price to today’s sales.
Sold at 97.1% of asking — spring comparables now run high.
If you’re buying
Condo? Start below asking.
7 in 8 sold at or below asking. The $520,000 median is a 2026 low.
Semi? Set your ceiling first.
More than 1 in 3 sold over asking — decide your number before offer night.
Detached? Negotiate.
4 in 5 sold at or below asking, at 98.1% of list.

What We’re Watching

Rates are on hold — but borrowing is getting pricier

Best 5-yr fixed
4.59%
insured · 5.09% conventional
  
Best 5-yr var.
3.41%
prime − 1.04%
  
BoC rate
2.25%
held Sep 2 · next Oct 28

Ontario rates as of Oct 9, 2026 (nesto). Your rate depends on your file.

What happened
The Bank of Canada held at 2.25% on September 2 — its seventh straight hold. Since then, high oil prices have kept inflation stubborn and the U.S. Fed has raised rates for the first time in over three years. Markets that priced a near-certain hold in early September now see a real chance of a hike on October 28. Five-year bond yields also rose about 0.20 points in the past month — and fixed mortgage rates follow bonds, not the Bank.
Our take
A “hold” isn’t relief. Buying in the next few months? Get a pre-approval with a rate hold now — most lenders hold a rate for 90–120 days. Renewing in 2027? Start the conversation four to six months out. With hikes back on the table, fixed vs. variable is a closer call than it was in the spring.
